title: What does it mean to be born again?
paragraphs: Understanding the Meaning of Being "Born Again"

Few concepts are as central to the Christian faith as being "born again." This phrase, made famous by Jesus' conversation with Nicodemus in John 3, captures the essence of the new life offered through faith in Christ. But what does it truly mean to be born again, and why is it so vital for every believer?
The Origin of the Term "Born Again"
The term "born again" comes directly from Jesus' teaching:
Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except one be born anew, he cannot see the kingdom of God. - John 3:3 ASV

Nicodemus, a Pharisee and religious leader, was puzzled by Jesus’ words, asking how a grown man could be born a second time (John 3:4 ASV). Jesus clarified that He was speaking of a spiritual rebirth, not a physical one:
That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit. - John 3:6 ASV
The Necessity of the New Birth

According to Jesus, being born again is not optional—it is essential for entering God’s kingdom. Human effort, religious background, or moral living cannot substitute for this spiritual birth. The new birth is necessary because all people are born with a sinful nature, separated from God (Romans 3:23 ASV).
How Are We Born Again?
Scripture teaches that the new birth is a work of God accomplished by the Holy Spirit. It occurs when a person responds to the gospel in repentance and faith. Consider these key passages:

But as many as received him, to them gave he the right to become children of God, even to them that believe on his name: who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God. - John 1:12-13 ASV
For by grace have ye been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God. - Ephesians 2:8 ASV
We are born again when we believe in Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior, trusting in His death and resurrection for the forgiveness of our sins (Romans 10:9 ASV).
The Evidence of New Birth
Being born again leads to a transformed life. The apostle Paul describes believers as "new creatures":
Wherefore if any man is in Christ, he is a new creature: the old things are passed away; behold, they are become new. - 2 Corinthians 5:17 ASV
This transformation includes:
A new relationship with God as Father (Romans 8:15 ASV)
A desire to turn away from sin (1 John 3:9 ASV)
The indwelling of the Holy Spirit (Galatians 5:22 ASV)
Love for other believers (1 John 4:7 ASV)
Different Perspectives

While some debate the relationship between being born again and baptism, mainline evangelical interpretation holds that the new birth is entirely a work of the Spirit, received by faith and not by any human ritual or effort. Baptism is seen as an outward sign of the inward change wrought by the Spirit (Acts 2:38 ASV), but not the means by which one is born again.
Conclusion

To be born again is to receive spiritual life from God by grace through faith in Jesus Christ. It is a radical, inward transformation that marks the beginning of a new relationship with God and the hope of eternal life.
